content: Cephradine is a cephalosporin antibiotic prescribed to treat bacterial infections, including pneumonia, as well as infections of the ear, skin, throat, and urinary tract. It is not effective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Cephradine is available in capsule and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken every 6 hours (four times a day) or every 12 hours (twice a day) for a duration of 7 to 10 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take cephradine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. Shake the liquid form well before each use to ensure even mixing. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Continue taking cephradine even if you feel better, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking cephradine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to cephradine, other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cefadroxil or cephalexin), penicillin, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), probenecid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, colitis, or stomach problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking cephradine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking cephradine. Take cephradine at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Cephradine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects requiring immediate medical attention include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, unusual bleeding or bruising, sore throat, painful mouth or throat sores, and vaginal infections. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store cephradine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Capsules should be stored at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Discard any outdated or unused medication. Liquid cephradine should be refrigerated, tightly closed, and discarded after 14 days. Do not freeze the liquid. It can also be stored at room temperature for up to 7 days. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal of unused medication. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to cephradine. If you have diabetes, consult your doctor before changing your diet or medication dosage. Use Clinistix or TesTape (not Clinitest) to test your urine for sugar while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the course of cephradine, contact your doctor.
